description: Curated structural knowledge graph of hazard -> system disruption and system -> system propagation. Reference-class knowledge (scientific literature and official open data practice), NOT a loss model. Used by src/climate/cascading.py to select cascade paths relevant to a location's REAL active hazards and REAL mapped exposure anchors.
not_quantified_statement: Propagation likelihoods and losses are NOT quantified — this is a structural relevance graph, not a loss model.
evidence_note: Every edge carries an evidence_class: SCIENTIFIC (mechanism established in the scientific literature, e.g. IPCC AR6 WG2 compound/cascading risk chapters) or OPEN_DATA_OFFICIAL (dependency documented in official/open-data infrastructure practice). quantified is always false: no edge carries a likelihood or loss figure.

edges.mechanism: Flame, heat and smoke damage lines and substations; operators may pre-emptively de-energise lines in high fire danger.
Fire, smoke and falling debris force road closures and can cut evacuation routes.
Flames and heat destroy crops, pasture and livestock; smoke taints produce.
Fire danger and smoke close natural areas and deter visitors.
Floodwater inundates and erodes road surfaces, cutting road links.
Floodwater undermines track beds and bridges, closing lines.
Flooding damages intake and treatment infrastructure and contaminates supplies.
Inundation damages facilities and blocks patient and staff access.
Prolonged inundation waterlogs crops and erodes topsoil.
Inundation damages industrial sites and forces shutdowns.
Extended precipitation deficit depletes reservoirs and groundwater, constraining supply.
Soil-moisture deficit stresses rain-fed crops and pasture.
Low reservoir levels and warm rivers constrain hydropower and thermal-plant cooling.
Peak cooling demand rises while lines and transformers derate in high temperatures.
Heat illness raises admissions, stressing emergency care.
Rail buckling risk rises in extreme heat, forcing speed restrictions and closures.
Heat forces closures or degraded conditions in non-cooled school buildings.
Heat stress cuts yields and raises livestock mortality risk.
Windthrow of trees and poles and line galloping cause outages.
Fallen trees and debris block roads; high-profile vehicles are restricted.
Wind damages overhead lines and mast infrastructure.
Extreme still-water levels and waves disrupt port operations and damage quays.
Coastal flooding and erosion cut coastal roads.
Beach erosion and coastal flooding degrade tourism assets.
Outages force hospitals onto backup power; prolonged loss degrades care.
Pumping and treatment depend on power; outages interrupt supply.
Towers and exchanges have limited battery backup; outages degrade networks.
Electrified lines and signalling stop without power.
Outages halt trading, cold chains and production.
Hospitals cannot operate safely without water.
Irrigation draws on supplies that are constrained in drought.
Road closures reroute and delay freight.
Rail closures shift freight onto constrained road capacity.
Port disruption breaks import and export chains.
Supply delays halt production and retail.
Loss of communications disrupts payments, coordination and remote work.
Crop losses propagate to food processing and farm income.
Tourism disruption cuts local business revenue.
Industrial disruption propagates to suppliers and customers.
